scorpio: SCORPIO (also: Study 178-CL-046, Mirabegron European-Australian phase 3); NCT00689104. Primary report: Khullar V, Amarenco G, Angulo JC, et al. Efficacy and tolerability of mirabegron, a β(3)-adrenoceptor agonist, in patients with overactive bladder: results from a randomised European-Australian phase 3 trial. *Eur Urol.* 2013;63(2):283-95. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2012.10.016 PMID:23182126. Compared: Mirabegron 50 or 100 mg vs placebo vs tolterodine ER, 12 weeks. Why it matters: Mirabegron registration trial (FDA 2012); AUA OAB 2024 and EAU cite it for β3-agonist efficacy. No WARWIKI page cites it. Note: Acronyms SCORPIO, CAPRICORN and TAURUS appear in review literature (e.g., Vij 2015) but not in these abstracts; trial-to-acronym mapping is from author knowledge.
aries: ARIES (also: Study 178-CL-047, Mirabegron North American phase 3). Primary report: Nitti VW, Auerbach S, Martin N, et al. Results of a randomized phase III trial of mirabegron in patients with overactive bladder. *J Urol.* 2013;189(4):1388-95. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.10.017 PMID:23079373. Compared: Mirabegron 50 or 100 mg vs placebo, 12 weeks. Why it matters: Mirabegron North American registration trial (FDA 2012); cited in AUA OAB 2024.
capricorn: CAPRICORN (also: Study 178-CL-074); NCT00912964. Primary report: Herschorn S, Barkin J, Castro-Diaz D, et al. A phase III, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, multicentre study to assess the efficacy and safety of the β₃ adrenoceptor agonist, mirabegron, in patients with symptoms of overactive bladder. *Urology.* 2013;82(2):313-20. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2013.02.077 PMID:23769122. Compared: Mirabegron 25 or 50 mg vs placebo, 12 weeks. Why it matters: Third 12-week mirabegron registration trial (25 and 50 mg; FDA 2012); cited in AUA OAB 2024. Note: Acronym not stated in the PubMed abstract; mapping from author knowledge (see scorpio note).
taurus: TAURUS (also: Study 178-CL-049, Mirabegron 12-month safety study); NCT00688688. Primary report: Chapple CR, Kaplan SA, Mitcheson D, et al. Randomized double-blind, active-controlled phase 3 study to assess 12-month safety and efficacy of mirabegron, a β(3)-adrenoceptor agonist, in overactive bladder. *Eur Urol.* 2013;63(2):296-305. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2012.10.048 PMID:23195283. Compared: Mirabegron 50 or 100 mg vs tolterodine ER, 12 months. Why it matters: 12-month mirabegron safety registration trial against tolterodine (FDA 2012); cited in AUA OAB 2024 and EAU. Note: Acronym not stated in the PubMed abstract; mapping from author knowledge (see scorpio note).
pillar: PILLAR (also: Mirabegron in patients aged 65 years or older). Primary report: Wagg A, Staskin D, Engel E, et al. Efficacy, safety, and tolerability of mirabegron in patients aged ≥65yr with overactive bladder wet: a phase IV, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study (PILLAR). *Eur Urol.* 2020;77(2):211-220. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2019.10.002 PMID:31733990. Compared: Mirabegron vs placebo in adults 65 or older. Why it matters: Mirabegron in adults 65 or older; AUA OAB 2024 cites it for β3 agonists in older patients.
plus: PLUS (also: Mirabegron add-on to tamsulosin in men). Primary report: Kaplan SA, Herschorn S, McVary KT, et al. Efficacy and Safety of Mirabegron versus Placebo Add-On Therapy in Men with Overactive Bladder Symptoms Receiving Tamsulosin for Underlying Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: A Randomized, Phase 4 Study (PLUS). *J Urol.* 2020;203(6):1163-1171. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000000738 PMID:31895002. Compared: Mirabegron vs placebo added to tamsulosin in men. Why it matters: Mirabegron add-on in men on tamsulosin; cited in AUA BPH 2026 and EAU male LUTS 2026 for add-on therapy.
times: TIMES (also: Tolterodine and tamsulosin in men with LUTS and OAB); NCT00147654. Primary report: Kaplan SA, Roehrborn CG, Rovner ES, et al. Tolterodine and tamsulosin for treatment of men with lower urinary tract symptoms and overactive bladder: a randomized controlled trial. *JAMA.* 2006;296(19):2319-28. doi:10.1001/jama.296.19.2319 PMID:17105794. Compared: Tolterodine ER, tamsulosin, both, or placebo in men. Why it matters: Tolterodine plus tamsulosin in men with LUTS and OAB; EAU male LUTS 2026 cites it for antimuscarinic add-on in men.
solifenacin-pivotal: Solifenacin pivotal trials (also: Cardozo 2004, Chapple 2004). Primary report: Cardozo L, Lisec M, Millard R, et al. Randomized, double-blind placebo controlled trial of the once daily antimuscarinic agent solifenacin succinate in patients with overactive bladder. *J Urol.* 2004;172(5 Pt 1):1919-24. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000140729.07840.16 PMID:15540755. Later reports: Chapple CR, Rechberger T, Al-Shukri S, et al. Randomized, double-blind placebo- and tolterodine-controlled trial of the once-daily antimuscarinic agent solifenacin in patients with symptomatic overactive bladder. *BJU Int.* 2004;93(3):303-10. doi:10.1111/j.1464-410x.2004.04606.x PMID:14764127. Compared: Solifenacin 5 or 10 mg vs placebo (and tolterodine). Why it matters: Solifenacin registration trials (FDA 2004); no solifenacin trial is in the library.
fesoterodine-pivotal: Fesoterodine pivotal trials (also: Chapple 2007, Nitti 2007). Primary report: Chapple C, Van Kerrebroeck P, Tubaro A, et al. Clinical efficacy, safety, and tolerability of once-daily fesoterodine in subjects with overactive bladder. *Eur Urol.* 2007;52(4):1204-12. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2007.07.009 PMID:17651893. Later reports: Nitti VW, Dmochowski R, Sand PK, et al. Efficacy, safety and tolerability of fesoterodine for overactive bladder syndrome. *J Urol.* 2007;178(6):2488-94. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2007.08.033 PMID:17937959. Compared: Fesoterodine 4 or 8 mg vs placebo (and tolterodine ER). Why it matters: Fesoterodine registration trials (FDA 2008); EAU female LUTS cites the fesoterodine program.
trospium-pivotal: Trospium pivotal trials (also: Zinner 2004, Rudy 2006). Primary report: Zinner N, Gittelman M, Harris R, et al. Trospium chloride improves overactive bladder symptoms: a multicenter phase III trial. *J Urol.* 2004;171(6 Pt 1):2311-5. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000127742.73136.0c PMID:15126811. Later reports: Rudy D, Cline K, Harris R, et al. Multicenter phase III trial studying trospium chloride in patients with overactive bladder. *Urology.* 2006;67(2):275-80. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2005.08.017 PMID:16461077. Compared: Trospium 20 mg twice daily vs placebo. Why it matters: Trospium US phase 3 registration trials (FDA 2004).
darifenacin-pivotal: Darifenacin pivotal trial (also: Haab 2004). Primary report: Haab F, Stewart L, Dwyer P. Darifenacin, an M3 selective receptor antagonist, is an effective and well-tolerated once-daily treatment for overactive bladder. *Eur Urol.* 2004;45(4):420-9. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2004.01.008 PMID:15041104. Compared: Darifenacin vs placebo. Why it matters: Darifenacin registration trial (FDA 2004), the M3-selective antimuscarinic.
tolterodine-er: Tolterodine extended-release pivotal trial (also: Van Kerrebroeck 2001). Primary report: Van Kerrebroeck P, Kreder K, Jonas U, et al. Tolterodine once-daily: superior efficacy and tolerability in the treatment of the overactive bladder. *Urology.* 2001;57(3):414-21. doi:10.1016/s0090-4295(00)01113-4 PMID:11248608. Compared: Tolterodine ER vs tolterodine IR vs placebo. Why it matters: Tolterodine ER registration trial (FDA 2000); tolterodine ER is the comparator in OrBIT, TAURUS and STAR.
oxybutynin-transdermal: Transdermal oxybutynin pivotal trials (also: Oxytrol, Dmochowski 2002, Dmochowski 2003). Primary report: Dmochowski RR, Davila GW, Zinner NR, et al. Efficacy and safety of transdermal oxybutynin in patients with urge and mixed urinary incontinence. *J Urol.* 2002;168(2):580-6. doi:None PMID:12131314. Later reports: Dmochowski RR, Sand PK, Zinner NR, et al. Comparative efficacy and safety of transdermal oxybutynin and oral tolterodine versus placebo in previously treated patients with urge and mixed urinary incontinence. *Urology.* 2003;62(2):237-42. doi:10.1016/s0090-4295(03)00356-x PMID:12893326. Compared: Transdermal oxybutynin vs placebo (and oral tolterodine). Why it matters: Transdermal oxybutynin registration trials (Oxytrol, FDA 2003). Note: Dmochowski 2002 has no DOI in PubMed.
oxybutynin-gel: Oxybutynin chloride topical gel pivotal trial (also: Gelnique, Staskin 2009). Primary report: Staskin DR, Dmochowski RR, Sand PK, et al. Efficacy and safety of oxybutynin chloride topical gel for overactive bladder: a randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, multicenter study. *J Urol.* 2009;181(4):1764-72. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2008.11.125 PMID:19233423. Compared: Oxybutynin gel vs placebo gel. Why it matters: Oxybutynin gel registration trial (FDA 2009).
opera: OPERA (also: Overactive Bladder: Performance of Extended Release Agents). Primary report: Diokno AC, Appell RA, Sand PK, et al. Prospective, randomized, double-blind study of the efficacy and tolerability of the extended-release formulations of oxybutynin and tolterodine for overactive bladder: results of the OPERA trial. *Mayo Clin Proc.* 2003;78(6):687-95. doi:10.4065/78.6.687 PMID:12934777. Compared: Oxybutynin ER vs tolterodine IR. Why it matters: Head-to-head oxybutynin ER versus tolterodine ER in women; widely taught class comparison.
star-solifenacin: STAR (also: Solifenacin versus tolterodine ER (STAR)). Primary report: Chapple CR, Martinez-Garcia R, Selvaggi L, et al. A comparison of the efficacy and tolerability of solifenacin succinate and extended release tolterodine at treating overactive bladder syndrome: results of the STAR trial. *Eur Urol.* 2005;48(3):464-70. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2005.05.015 PMID:15990220. Compared: Solifenacin vs tolterodine ER. Why it matters: Head-to-head solifenacin versus tolterodine ER (flexible dose).
fesoterodine-vs-tolterodine: Fesoterodine versus tolterodine ER head-to-head (also: Herschorn 2010). Primary report: Herschorn S, Swift S, Guan Z, et al. Comparison of fesoterodine and tolterodine extended release for the treatment of overactive bladder: a head-to-head placebo-controlled trial. *BJU Int.* 2010;105(1):58-66. doi:10.1111/j.1464-410X.2009.09086.x PMID:20132103. Compared: Fesoterodine 8 mg vs tolterodine ER vs placebo. Why it matters: Head-to-head fesoterodine versus tolterodine ER; cited in EAU female LUTS 2026.
sofia: SOFIA (also: Fesoterodine in vulnerable elderly); NCT00928070. Primary report: Dubeau CE, Kraus SR, Griebling TL, et al. Effect of fesoterodine in vulnerable elderly subjects with urgency incontinence: a double-blind, placebo controlled trial. *J Urol.* 2014;191(2):395-404. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2013.08.027 PMID:23973522. Compared: Fesoterodine vs placebo in vulnerable elderly. Why it matters: Fesoterodine in vulnerable elderly; EAU female LUTS 2026 cites it for antimuscarinics in older adults.
senior: SENIOR (also: Solifenacin and oxybutynin cognition in mild cognitive impairment); NCT01126424. Primary report: Wagg A, Dale M, Tretter R, et al. Randomised, multicentre, placebo-controlled, double-blind crossover study investigating the effect of solifenacin and oxybutynin in elderly people with mild cognitive impairment: the SENIOR study. *Eur Urol.* 2013;64(1):74-81. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2013.01.002 PMID:23332882. Compared: Solifenacin vs oxybutynin vs placebo, cognition in MCI. Why it matters: Cognitive safety of solifenacin versus oxybutynin in mild cognitive impairment; cited in EAU female LUTS 2026.
neptune: NEPTUNE (also: Solifenacin plus tamsulosin OCAS fixed-dose combination); NCT01018511. Primary report: van Kerrebroeck P, Chapple C, Drogendijk T, et al. Combination therapy with solifenacin and tamsulosin oral controlled absorption system in a single tablet for lower urinary tract symptoms in men: efficacy and safety results from the randomised controlled NEPTUNE trial. *Eur Urol.* 2013;64(6):1003-12. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2013.07.034 PMID:23932438. Compared: Solifenacin plus tamsulosin OCAS vs tamsulosin vs placebo. Why it matters: Fixed-dose solifenacin plus tamsulosin in men with storage and voiding LUTS; cited in EAU male LUTS 2026.
tolterodine-boo-safety: Tolterodine safety in men with bladder outlet obstruction (also: Abrams 2006). Primary report: Abrams P, Kaplan S, De Koning Gans HJ, et al. Safety and tolerability of tolterodine for the treatment of overactive bladder in men with bladder outlet obstruction. *J Urol.* 2006;175(3 Pt 1):999-1004. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(05)00483-0 PMID:16469601. Compared: Tolterodine vs placebo in men with BOO (retention safety). Why it matters: Retention safety of tolterodine in men with urodynamic BOO; EAU male LUTS 2026 cites it.
burgio-2020-men: Burgio 2020 combined behavioral and drug therapy in men (also: Burgio 2020, 3-site, 2-stage, 3-arm RCT in men); NCT01175382. Primary report: Burgio KL, Kraus SR, Johnson TM 2nd, et al. Effectiveness of Combined Behavioral and Drug Therapy for Overactive Bladder Symptoms in Men: A Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA Intern Med.* 2020;180(3):411-419. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2019.6398 PMID:31930360. Compared: Behavioral therapy plus drug vs drug alone in men. Why it matters: Behavioral plus drug therapy for OAB in men; cited in AUA OAB 2024, AUA BPH 2026 and EAU male LUTS 2026. Note: WARWIKI calls a Burgio trial 'COBALT'; that name is not in the PubMed record, so it is not used here.
motive: MOTIVE (also: Male Overactive Bladder Treatment in Veterans); NCT01187498. Primary report: Burgio KL, Goode PS, Johnson TM, et al. Behavioral versus drug treatment for overactive bladder in men: the Male Overactive Bladder Treatment in Veterans (MOTIVE) Trial. *J Am Geriatr Soc.* 2011;59(12):2209-16. doi:10.1111/j.1532-5415.2011.03724.x PMID:22092152. Compared: Behavioral therapy vs oxybutynin in men. Why it matters: Behavioral therapy versus drug therapy for OAB in men (veterans); AUA BPH 2026 cites it.
be-dri: BE-DRI (also: Behavior Enhances Drug Reduction of Incontinence, UITN); NCT00090584. Primary report: Burgio KL, Kraus SR, Menefee S, et al. Behavioral therapy to enable women with urge incontinence to discontinue drug treatment: a randomized trial. *Ann Intern Med.* 2008;149(3):161-9. doi:10.7326/0003-4819-149-3-200808050-00005 PMID:18678843. Compared: Drug plus behavioral therapy vs drug alone, then drug discontinuation. Why it matters: UITN trial of behavioral therapy to allow drug discontinuation in women with urge incontinence (negative).
nocdurna-pivotal: Low-dose desmopressin ODT pivotal trials (also: Nocdurna, Weiss 2013 (men), Sand 2013 (women)). Primary report: Weiss JP, Herschorn S, Albei CD, et al. Efficacy and safety of low dose desmopressin orally disintegrating tablet in men with nocturia: results of a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, parallel group study. *J Urol.* 2013;190(3):965-72. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.12.112 PMID:23454402. Later reports: Sand PK, Dmochowski RR, Reddy J, et al. Efficacy and safety of low dose desmopressin orally disintegrating tablet in women with nocturia: results of a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, parallel group study. *J Urol.* 2013;190(3):958-64. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2013.02.037 PMID:23454404. Compared: Low-dose desmopressin ODT vs placebo (men; women). Why it matters: Low-dose desmopressin registration trials in men and women (Nocdurna, FDA 2018); cited in EAU male LUTS 2026. No nocturia trial is in the library. Note: Two parallel trials (men, women) of one program.
noctupus: Desmopressin (Minirin) nocturia trials in men and women (also: Mattiasson 2002 (men), Lose 2003 (women), NOCTUPUS (name not confirmed in PubMed)). Primary report: Mattiasson A, Abrams P, Van Kerrebroeck P, et al. Efficacy of desmopressin in the treatment of nocturia: a double-blind placebo-controlled study in men. *BJU Int.* 2002;89(9):855-62. doi:10.1046/j.1464-410x.2002.02791.x PMID:12010228. Later reports: Lose G, Lalos O, Freeman RM, et al. Efficacy of desmopressin (Minirin) in the treatment of nocturia: a double-blind placebo-controlled study in women. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2003;189(4):1106-13. doi:10.1067/s0002-9378(03)00593-3 PMID:14586363. Compared: Desmopressin vs placebo (men; women). Why it matters: Original desmopressin nocturia trials in men and women; EAU female LUTS 2026 cites the women's trial.
noctiva-pivotal: SER120 (Noctiva) pivotal trials (also: DB3, DB4, desmopressin nasal spray). Primary report: Kaminetsky J, Fein S, Dmochowski R, et al. Efficacy and Safety of SER120 Nasal Spray in Patients with Nocturia: Pooled Analysis of 2 Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled, Phase 3 Trials. *J Urol.* 2018;200(3):604-611. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2018.04.050 PMID:29654805. Compared: Desmopressin nasal spray vs placebo (pooled DB3/DB4). Why it matters: Desmopressin nasal spray registration trials (Noctiva, FDA 2017); WARWIKI discusses the NOCTIVA label.
chapple-oab-botox: Chapple OnabotulinumtoxinA OAB phase 3 (also: Allergan 191622-520, EMBARK program second pivotal); NCT00910520. Primary report: Chapple C, Sievert KD, MacDiarmid S, et al. OnabotulinumtoxinA 100 U significantly improves all idiopathic overactive bladder symptoms and quality of life in patients with overactive bladder and urinary incontinence: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. *Eur Urol.* 2013;64(2):249-56. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2013.04.001 PMID:23608668. Compared: OnabotulinumtoxinA 100 U vs placebo, idiopathic OAB. Why it matters: Second 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA registration trial for idiopathic OAB (FDA 2013), the twin of nitti-oab; cited in AUA OAB 2024 and EAU.
botox-oab-dose-ranging: OnabotulinumtoxinA idiopathic OAB dose-ranging trial (also: Dmochowski 2010). Primary report: Dmochowski R, Chapple C, Nitti VW, et al. Efficacy and safety of onabotulinumtoxinA for idiopathic overactive bladder: a double-blind, placebo controlled, randomized, dose ranging trial. *J Urol.* 2010;184(6):2416-22. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2010.08.021 PMID:20952013. Compared: OnabotulinumtoxinA 50 to 300 U vs placebo. Why it matters: Phase 2 dose-ranging trial that set 100 U for idiopathic OAB; cited in AUA OAB 2024.
botox-vs-solifenacin: OnabotulinumtoxinA or solifenacin versus placebo phase 3b (also: Herschorn 2017). Primary report: Herschorn S, Kohan A, Aliotta P, et al. The Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA or Solifenacin Compared with Placebo in Solifenacin Naïve Patients with Refractory Overactive Bladder: Results from a Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind Phase 3b Trial. *J Urol.* 2017;198(1):167-175. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2017.01.069 PMID:28161352. Compared: OnabotulinumtoxinA vs solifenacin vs placebo. Why it matters: Phase 3b onabotulinumtoxinA versus solifenacin versus placebo; cited in AUA OAB 2024.
cruz-ndo: Cruz NDO OnabotulinumtoxinA phase 3 (also: DIGNITY, Allergan 191622-516); NCT00461292. Primary report: Cruz F, Herschorn S, Aliotta P, et al. Efficacy and safety of onabotulinumtoxinA in patients with urinary incontinence due to neurogenic detrusor overactivity: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. *Eur Urol.* 2011;60(4):742-50. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2011.07.002 PMID:21798658. Compared: OnabotulinumtoxinA 200 or 300 U vs placebo, NDO. Why it matters: Second NDO registration trial (DIGNITY 516; FDA 2011), the twin of ginsberg-ndo; cited in AUA/SUFU NLUTD 2021; 4 WARWIKI pages cite it.
schurch-ndo: Schurch botulinum toxin A NDO trial (also: Schurch 2005). Primary report: Schurch B, de Sèze M, Denys P, et al. Botulinum toxin type a is a safe and effective treatment for neurogenic urinary incontinence: results of a single treatment, randomized, placebo controlled 6-month study. *J Urol.* 2005;174(1):196-200. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000162035.73977.1c PMID:15947626. Compared: Botulinum toxin A 200 or 300 U vs placebo, NDO. Why it matters: First multicenter placebo-controlled botulinum toxin A trial in NDO; cited in EAU neuro-urology 2026.
botox-ms-100u: Low-dose OnabotulinumtoxinA in noncatheterizing MS (also: Tullman 2018); NCT01600716. Primary report: Tullman M, Chartier-Kastler E, Kohan A, et al. Low-dose onabotulinumtoxinA improves urinary symptoms in noncatheterizing patients with MS. *Neurology.* 2018;91(7):e657-e665. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000005991 PMID:30030330. Compared: OnabotulinumtoxinA 100 U vs placebo, MS without catheterization. Why it matters: 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA in noncatheterizing MS patients; cited in AUA/SUFU NLUTD 2021 and EAU neuro-urology 2026.
interstim-pivotal: InterStim pivotal trials (Sacral Nerve Stimulation Study Group) (also: MDT-103, Schmidt 1999, Hassouna 2000, Jonas 2001). Primary report: Schmidt RA, Jonas U, Oleson KA, et al. Sacral nerve stimulation for treatment of refractory urinary urge incontinence. Sacral Nerve Stimulation Study Group. *J Urol.* 1999;162(2):352-7. doi:None PMID:10411037. Later reports: Hassouna MM, Siegel SW, Nÿeholt AA, et al. Sacral neuromodulation in the treatment of urgency-frequency symptoms: a multicenter study on efficacy and safety. *J Urol.* 2000;163(6):1849-54. PMID:10799197 | Jonas U, Fowler CJ, Chancellor MB, et al. Efficacy of sacral nerve stimulation for urinary retention: results 18 months after implantation. *J Urol.* 2001;165(1):15-9. doi:10.1097/00005392-200101000-00004 PMID:11125353 | van Kerrebroeck PE, van Voskuilen AC, Heesakkers JP, et al. Results of sacral neuromodulation therapy for urinary voiding dysfunction: outcomes of a prospective, worldwide clinical study. *J Urol.* 2007;178(5):2029-34. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2007.07.032 PMID:17869298. Compared: Sacral nerve stimulation implant vs delayed implant/standard care. Why it matters: Sacral Nerve Stimulation Study Group trials behind FDA approval of InterStim (urge incontinence 1997; urgency-frequency and retention 1999); EAU cites Schmidt 1999. Note: One multicenter study (MDT-103) reported by indication; Schmidt 1999 and Hassouna 2000 have no DOI in PubMed.
ecoin-pivotal: eCoin pivotal study (also: Leadless tibial nerve stimulator pivotal). Primary report: Rogers A, Bragg S, Ferrante K, et al. Pivotal Study of Leadless Tibial Nerve Stimulation with eCoin® for Urgency Urinary Incontinence: An Open-Label, Single Arm Trial. *J Urol.* 2021;206(2):399-408. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000001733 PMID:33797291. Later reports: Lucente V, Giusto L, MacDiarmid S. Two-year Pivotal Study Analysis of the Safety and Efficacy of Implantable Tibial Nerve Stimulation With eCoin® for Urgency Urinary Incontinence. *Urology.* 2024;194:17-23. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2024.07.046 PMID:39089497. Compared: Leadless tibial stimulator, single arm. Why it matters: Registration trial for the leadless eCoin tibial stimulator (FDA 2022); cited in AUA OAB 2024; 3 WARWIKI pages cite it. Note: Single-arm pivotal (FDA P200036 per WARWIKI ecoin.mdx).
titan-2: TITAN 2 (also: Medtronic implantable tibial neuromodulation pivotal, Altaviva). Primary report: Lee U, Xavier K, Carey J, et al. Implantable Tibial Neuromodulation Therapy Improves Symptoms of Urge Urinary Incontinence From the TITAN 2 Pivotal Study. *J Urol.* 2026;215(6):702-712. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000004958 PMID:41587348. Compared: Implantable tibial neuromodulation, single arm. Why it matters: Registration study for Medtronic's implantable tibial neuromodulation system (Altaviva, FDA September 2025); 3 WARWIKI pages cite it. Note: Single-arm pivotal; FDA approval of Altaviva on September 18, 2025 per WARWIKI altaviva.mdx.
intibia-sham: Intibia sham-controlled trial (also: Intibia System). Primary report: Mangel J, Miller K, Erickson T, et al. Randomized, Sham-Controlled, Double-Blind Trial of the Intibia System in Urge Urinary Incontinence: Quality-of-Life Outcomes. *Int Urogynecol J.* 2026;37(10):3621-3630. doi:10.1007/s00192-026-06636-1 PMID:42329399. Compared: Implantable tibial stimulation vs sham. Why it matters: First sham-controlled RCT of an implantable tibial nerve system; 4 WARWIKI pages cite it. Note: Only the quality-of-life report is indexed so far; the primary efficacy report was not found in PubMed (November 11, 2026).
ptns-sham-finazzi: Finazzi-Agrò PTNS versus sham (also: Finazzi-Agrò 2010). Primary report: Finazzi-Agrò E, Petta F, Sciobica F, et al. Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation effects on detrusor overactivity incontinence are not due to a placebo effect: a randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled trial. *J Urol.* 2010;184(5):2001-6. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2010.06.113 PMID:20850833. Compared: PTNS vs sham. Why it matters: Sham-controlled PTNS trial with urodynamic outcomes; cited in EAU female LUTS 2026.
future: FUTURE (also: Female Urgency, Trial of Urodynamics as Routine Evaluation). Primary report: Abdel-Fattah M, Chapple C, Cooper D, et al. Invasive urodynamic investigations in the management of women with refractory overactive bladder symptoms (FUTURE) in the UK: a multicentre, superiority, parallel, open-label, randomised controlled trial. *Lancet.* 2025;405(10484):1057-1068. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01886-5 PMID:40132616. Later reports: Abdel-Fattah M, Chapple C, Breeman S, et al. Invasive urodynamic investigations in the management of women with refractory overactive bladder symptoms: FUTURE, a superiority RCT and economic evaluation. *Health Technol Assess.* 2025;29(27):1-139. doi:10.3310/UKYW4923 PMID:40620147. Compared: Urodynamics plus clinical assessment vs clinical assessment alone before third-line OAB therapy. Why it matters: UK RCT of invasive urodynamics before third-line treatment of refractory OAB in women (Lancet 2025); EAU female LUTS cites the protocol; 3 WARWIKI pages cite it.
pride: PRIDE (also: Program to Reduce Incontinence by Diet and Exercise); NCT00091988. Primary report: Subak LL, Wing R, West DS, et al. Weight loss to treat urinary incontinence in overweight and obese women. *N Engl J Med.* 2009;360(5):481-90. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa0806375 PMID:19179316. Compared: Behavioral weight-loss program vs structured education. Why it matters: Weight loss for incontinence in overweight women (NEJM 2009); cited in AUA OAB 2024 and EAU female LUTS 2026 for weight-loss advice.
vusis-ii: VUSIS-II (also: Value of Urodynamics before Stress urinary Incontinence Surgery II); NCT00814749. Primary report: van Leijsen SAL, Kluivers KB, Mol BWJ, et al. Value of urodynamics before stress urinary incontinence surgery: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2013;121(5):999-1008. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e31828c68e3 PMID:23635736. Compared: Urodynamics before SUI surgery vs no urodynamics (noninferiority). Why it matters: Dutch urodynamics-before-SUI-surgery RCT, the companion to VALUE; cited in EAU female LUTS 2026. Note: Name confirmed by Mengerink 2018 (VALUE/VUSIS-2); not stated in the abstract.
musa: MUSA (also: Midurethral Sling vs OnabotulinumtoxinA, PFDN MUSA); NCT04171531. Primary report: Harvie HS, Menefee SA, Richter HE, et al. Midurethral Sling vs OnabotulinumtoxinA in Females With Urinary Incontinence: The MUSA Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA.* 2025;333(21):1887-1896. doi:10.1001/jama.2025.4682 PMID:40323617. Compared: Midurethral sling vs onabotulinumtoxinA, mixed incontinence. Why it matters: PFDN trial of midurethral sling versus onabotulinumtoxinA for mixed incontinence (JAMA 2025); 3 WARWIKI pages cite it.
bulkamid-pivotal: Bulkamid pivotal trial (also: Polyacrylamide hydrogel versus Contigen). Primary report: Sokol ER, Karram MM, Dmochowski R. Efficacy and safety of polyacrylamide hydrogel for the treatment of female stress incontinence: a randomized, prospective, multicenter North American study. *J Urol.* 2014;192(3):843-9. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2014.03.109 PMID:24704117. Compared: Polyacrylamide hydrogel vs collagen (Contigen). Why it matters: Polyacrylamide hydrogel registration trial (Bulkamid, FDA PMA 2020); 3 WARWIKI pages cite it.
macroplastique-pivotal: Macroplastique pivotal trial (also: Polydimethylsiloxane versus collagen). Primary report: Ghoniem G, Corcos J, Comiter C, et al. Cross-linked polydimethylsiloxane injection for female stress urinary incontinence: results of a multicenter, randomized, controlled, single-blind study. *J Urol.* 2009;181(1):204-10. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2008.09.032 PMID:19013613. Compared: Polydimethylsiloxane vs collagen. Why it matters: Polydimethylsiloxane registration trial (Macroplastique, FDA 2006); 2 WARWIKI pages cite it.
coaptite-pivotal: Coaptite pivotal trial (also: Calcium hydroxylapatite versus collagen). Primary report: Mayer RD, Dmochowski RR, Appell RA, et al. Multicenter prospective randomized 52-week trial of calcium hydroxylapatite versus bovine dermal collagen for treatment of stress urinary incontinence. *Urology.* 2007;69(5):876-80. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2007.01.050 PMID:17482925. Compared: Calcium hydroxylapatite vs collagen. Why it matters: Calcium hydroxylapatite registration trial (Coaptite, FDA 2005).
durasphere-pivotal: Durasphere pivotal trial (also: Carbon-coated beads versus collagen). Primary report: Lightner D, Calvosa C, Andersen R, et al. A new injectable bulking agent for treatment of stress urinary incontinence: results of a multicenter, randomized, controlled, double-blind study of Durasphere. *Urology.* 2001;58(1):12-5. doi:10.1016/s0090-4295(01)01148-7 PMID:11445471. Compared: Carbon-coated beads vs collagen. Why it matters: Carbon-coated bead registration trial (Durasphere, FDA 1999).
finnish-tvt-tvto: Finnish TVT versus TVT-O trial (also: Laurikainen 2007, Laurikainen 2014); NCT00379314. Primary report: Laurikainen E, Valpas A, Kivelä A, et al. Retropubic compared with transobturator tape placement in treatment of urinary incontinence: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2007;109(1):4-11. doi:10.1097/01.AOG.0000249607.82768.a1 PMID:17197581. Later reports: Laurikainen E, Valpas A, Aukee P, et al. Five-year results of a randomized trial comparing retropubic and transobturator midurethral slings for stress incontinence. *Eur Urol.* 2014;65(6):1109-14. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2014.01.031 PMID:24508070. Compared: Retropubic TVT vs TVT-O. Why it matters: Nordic retropubic versus transobturator trial with 5-year follow-up; AUA SUI 2023 cites the 5-year report.
schierlitz-isd: TVT versus TOT in intrinsic sphincter deficiency (also: Schierlitz 2008). Primary report: Schierlitz L, Dwyer PL, Rosamilia A, et al. Effectiveness of tension-free vaginal tape compared with transobturator tape in women with stress urinary incontinence and intrinsic sphincter deficiency: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2008;112(6):1253-1261. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e31818db391 PMID:19037033. Compared: TVT vs TOT in intrinsic sphincter deficiency. Why it matters: TVT versus TOT in women with intrinsic sphincter deficiency.
guerrero-sling-materials: TVT versus Pelvicol versus autologous fascial sling (also: Guerrero 2010). Primary report: Guerrero KL, Emery SJ, Wareham K, et al. A randomised controlled trial comparing TVT, Pelvicol and autologous fascial slings for the treatment of stress urinary incontinence in women. *BJOG.* 2010;117(12):1493-502. doi:10.1111/j.1471-0528.2010.02696.x PMID:20939862. Compared: TVT vs porcine dermis vs autologous fascial sling. Why it matters: TVT versus porcine dermis versus autologous fascia; cited in AUA SUI 2023 and EAU female LUTS 2026.
opal: OPAL (also: Optimal PFMT for Adult women's Lifetime, PFMT with versus without EMG biofeedback). Primary report: Hagen S, Elders A, Stratton S, et al. Effectiveness of pelvic floor muscle training with and without electromyographic biofeedback for urinary incontinence in women: multicentre randomised controlled trial. *BMJ.* 2020;371:m3719. doi:10.1136/bmj.m3719 PMID:33055247. Later reports: Hagen S, Bugge C, Dean SG, et al. Basic versus biofeedback-mediated intensive pelvic floor muscle training for women with urinary incontinence: the OPAL RCT. *Health Technol Assess.* 2020;24(70):1-144. doi:10.3310/hta24700 PMID:33289476. Compared: PFMT with vs without EMG biofeedback. Why it matters: UK trial showing EMG biofeedback adds nothing to supervised PFMT (BMJ 2020); EAU cites the HTA report.
bo-1999: Bø 1999 PFMT versus electrical stimulation versus cones (also: Bo 1999). Primary report: Bø K, Talseth T, Holme I. Single blind, randomised controlled trial of pelvic floor exercises, electrical stimulation, vaginal cones, and no treatment in management of genuine stress incontinence in women. *BMJ.* 1999;318(7182):487-93. doi:10.1136/bmj.318.7182.487 PMID:10024253. Compared: PFMT vs electrical stimulation vs cones vs no treatment. Why it matters: Classic PFMT versus electrical stimulation versus cones trial; cited in EAU female LUTS 2026.
goode-2003: Goode 2003 behavioral training with or without electrical stimulation (also: Goode 2003). Primary report: Goode PS, Burgio KL, Locher JL, et al. Effect of behavioral training with or without pelvic floor electrical stimulation on stress incontinence in women: a randomized controlled trial. *JAMA.* 2003;290(3):345-52. doi:10.1001/jama.290.3.345 PMID:12865375. Compared: Behavioral training with or without electrical stimulation vs self-help booklet. Why it matters: Behavioral training with or without electrical stimulation for SUI (JAMA 2003).
group-pfmt: Dumoulin group versus individual PFMT in older women (also: Dumoulin 2020); NCT02039830. Primary report: Dumoulin C, Morin M, Danieli C, et al. Group-Based vs Individual Pelvic Floor Muscle Training to Treat Urinary Incontinence in Older Women: A Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA Intern Med.* 2020;180(10):1284-1293. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2020.2993 PMID:32744599. Compared: Group-based vs individual PFMT in older women. Why it matters: Group-based PFMT noninferior to individual PFMT in older women; cited in EAU female LUTS 2026.
duloxetine-sui: Duloxetine North American SUI phase 3 (also: Dmochowski 2003). Primary report: Dmochowski RR, Miklos JR, Norton PA, et al. Duloxetine versus placebo for the treatment of North American women with stress urinary incontinence. *J Urol.* 2003;170(4 Pt 1):1259-63. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000080708.87092.cc PMID:14501737. Compared: Duloxetine 40 mg twice daily vs placebo. Why it matters: North American phase 3 duloxetine SUI trial (approved in Europe, not the US); basis for drug-therapy statements.
cupido-1: CUPIDO 1 (also: Prolapse repair with or without MUS in women with SUI). Primary report: van der Ploeg JM, Oude Rengerink K, van der Steen A, et al. Transvaginal prolapse repair with or without the addition of a midurethral sling in women with genital prolapse and stress urinary incontinence: a randomised trial. *BJOG.* 2015;122(7):1022-30. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.13325 PMID:25754458. Compared: Prolapse repair with vs without MUS, women with SUI. Why it matters: Prolapse repair with or without MUS in women with SUI; cited in EAU female LUTS 2026. Note: CUPIDO name confirmed by the trial protocol (van der Steen 2010).
cupido-2: CUPIDO 2 (also: Prolapse repair with or without MUS in women with occult SUI). Primary report: van der Ploeg JM, Oude Rengerink K, van der Steen A, et al. Vaginal prolapse repair with or without a midurethral sling in women with genital prolapse and occult stress urinary incontinence: a randomized trial. *Int Urogynecol J.* 2016;27(7):1029-38. doi:10.1007/s00192-015-2924-1 PMID:26740197. Compared: Prolapse repair with vs without MUS, occult SUI. Why it matters: Prolapse repair with or without MUS in women with occult SUI; cited in AUA SUI 2023 and EAU female LUTS 2026. Note: CUPIDO name confirmed by the trial protocol (van der Steen 2010).
trabuco-burch-sling: Burch versus midurethral sling at sacrocolpopexy (also: Trabuco 2016, Trabuco 2018). Primary report: Trabuco EC, Klingele CJ, Blandon RE, et al. Burch Retropubic Urethropexy Compared With Midurethral Sling With Concurrent Sacrocolpopexy: A Randomized Controlled Trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2016;128(4):828-35. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000001651 PMID:27607858. Later reports: Trabuco EC, Linder BJ, Klingele CJ, et al. Two-Year Results of Burch Compared With Midurethral Sling With Sacrocolpopexy: A Randomized Controlled Trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2018;131(1):31-38. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000002415 PMID:29215517. Compared: Burch vs retropubic MUS at sacrocolpopexy. Why it matters: Burch versus retropubic sling at sacrocolpopexy, the abdominal counterpart to CARE.
people: PEOPLE (also: Pessary or surgery for pelvic organ prolapse (randomized arm)). Primary report: van der Vaart LR, Vollebregt A, Milani AL, et al. Effect of Pessary vs Surgery on Patient-Reported Improvement in Patients With Symptomatic Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA.* 2022;328(23):2312-2323. doi:10.1001/jama.2022.22385 PMID:36538310. Compared: Pessary vs surgery as first treatment. Why it matters: Pessary versus surgery as first treatment for prolapse (JAMA 2022); 3 WARWIKI pages cite it. Note: Use the JAMA randomized report; the BJOG 2022 PEOPLE paper is a separate prospective cohort.
maher-2004: Maher 2004 abdominal sacrocolpopexy versus sacrospinous colpopexy (also: Maher 2004). Primary report: Maher CF, Qatawneh AM, Dwyer PL, et al. Abdominal sacral colpopexy or vaginal sacrospinous colpopexy for vaginal vault prolapse: a prospective randomized study. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2004;190(1):20-6. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2003.08.031 PMID:14749629. Compared: Abdominal sacrocolpopexy vs vaginal sacrospinous colpopexy (vault). Why it matters: Classic RCT of abdominal sacrocolpopexy versus vaginal sacrospinous colpopexy for vault prolapse.
benson-1996: Benson 1996 vaginal versus abdominal reconstructive surgery (also: Benson 1996). Primary report: Benson JT, Lucente V, McClellan E. Vaginal versus abdominal reconstructive surgery for the treatment of pelvic support defects: a prospective randomized study with long-term outcome evaluation. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 1996;175(6):1418-21. doi:10.1016/s0002-9378(96)70084-4 PMID:8987919. Compared: Vaginal vs abdominal reconstructive surgery. Why it matters: Early vaginal versus abdominal reconstructive surgery RCT.
salto-2: SALTO-2 (also: Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy versus sacrospinous fixation for vault prolapse). Primary report: van Oudheusden AMJ, van IJsselmuiden MN, Menge LF, et al. Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy versus vaginal sacrospinous fixation for vaginal vault prolapse: a randomised controlled trial and prospective cohort (SALTO-2 trial). *BJOG.* 2023;130(12):1542-1551. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.17525 PMID:37132094. Compared: Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy vs sacrospinous fixation (vault). Why it matters: Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy versus sacrospinous fixation for vault prolapse (BJOG 2023); 2 WARWIKI pages cite it.
maher-2011: Maher 2011 laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy versus total vaginal mesh (also: Maher 2011). Primary report: Maher CF, Feiner B, DeCuyper EM, et al. Laparoscopic sacral colpopexy versus total vaginal mesh for vaginal vault prolapse: a randomized trial. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;204(4):360.e1-7. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2010.11.016 PMID:21306698. Compared: Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy vs total vaginal mesh (vault). Why it matters: Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy versus total vaginal mesh for vault prolapse.
paraiso-lap-robotic: Paraiso laparoscopic versus robotic sacrocolpopexy (also: Paraiso 2011); NCT00551993. Primary report: Paraiso MFR, Jelovsek JE, Frick A, et al. Laparoscopic compared with robotic sacrocolpopexy for vaginal prolapse: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;118(5):1005-1013. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e318231537c PMID:21979458. Compared: Laparoscopic vs robotic sacrocolpopexy. Why it matters: Laparoscopic versus robotic sacrocolpopexy (time, cost, pain).
anger-robotic: Anger robotic versus laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy (also: Anger 2014); NCT01124916. Primary report: Anger JT, Mueller ER, Tarnay C, et al. Robotic compared with laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2014;123(1):5-12. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000000006 PMID:24463657. Compared: Robotic vs laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy. Why it matters: Robotic versus laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy cost trial.
salto: SALTO (also: Laparoscopic versus open sacrocolpopexy for vault prolapse). Primary report: Coolen AWM, van Oudheusden AMJ, Mol BWJ, et al. Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy compared with open abdominal sacrocolpopexy for vault prolapse repair: a randomised controlled trial. *Int Urogynecol J.* 2017;28(10):1469-1479. doi:10.1007/s00192-017-3296-5 PMID:28417153. Later reports: van Oudheusden AMJ, Eissing J, Terink IM, et al. Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy versus abdominal sacrocolpopexy for vaginal vault prolapse: long-term follow-up of a randomized controlled trial. *Int Urogynecol J.* 2023;34(1):93-104. doi:10.1007/s00192-022-05350-y PMID:36112182. Compared: Laparoscopic vs open sacrocolpopexy (vault). Why it matters: Laparoscopic versus open sacrocolpopexy for vault prolapse, with long-term follow-up. Note: Lap versus open sacrocolpopexy (SALTO); SALTO-2 is the lap sacrocolpopexy versus sacrospinous fixation trial.
lava: LAVA (also: Laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy versus vaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy). Primary report: van IJsselmuiden MN, van Oudheusden A, Veen J, et al. Hysteropexy in the treatment of uterine prolapse stage 2 or higher: laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy versus sacrospinous hysteropexy-a multicentre randomised controlled trial (LAVA trial). *BJOG.* 2020;127(10):1284-1293. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.16242 PMID:32267624. Compared: Laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy vs vaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy. Why it matters: Laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy versus vaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy; 2 WARWIKI pages cite it.
iglesia-mesh: Iglesia vaginal mesh trial (also: Iglesia 2010, Gutman 2013); NCT00475540. Primary report: Iglesia CB, Sokol AI, Sokol ER, et al. Vaginal mesh for prolapse: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2010;116(2 Pt 1):293-303. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e3181e7d7f8 PMID:20664388. Later reports: Gutman RE, Nosti PA, Sokol AI, et al. Three-year outcomes of vaginal mesh for prolapse: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2013;122(4):770-777. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e3182a49dac PMID:24084533. Compared: Vaginal mesh kit vs native-tissue colpopexy. Why it matters: US vaginal mesh RCT stopped early for mesh exposure.
withagen-recurrent: Withagen trocar-guided mesh in recurrent prolapse (also: Withagen 2011); NCT00372190. Primary report: Withagen MI, Milani AL, den Boon J, et al. Trocar-guided mesh compared with conventional vaginal repair in recurrent prolapse: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;117(2 Pt 1):242-250. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e318203e6a5 PMID:21252735. Compared: Trocar-guided mesh vs conventional repair, recurrent prolapse. Why it matters: Trocar-guided mesh versus native tissue for recurrent prolapse.
prospere: PROSPERE (also: Prosthetic Pelvic Floor Repair trial, Vaginal mesh versus laparoscopic sacropexy for cystocele). Primary report: Lucot JP, Cosson M, Bader G, et al. Safety of Vaginal Mesh Surgery Versus Laparoscopic Mesh Sacropexy for Cystocele Repair: Results of the Prosthetic Pelvic Floor Repair Randomized Controlled Trial. *Eur Urol.* 2018;74(2):167-176. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2018.01.044 PMID:29472143. Later reports: Lucot JP, Cosson M, Verdun S, et al. Long-term outcomes of primary cystocele repair by transvaginal mesh surgery versus laparoscopic mesh sacropexy: extended follow up of the PROSPERE multicentre randomised trial. *BJOG.* 2022;129(1):127-137. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.16847 PMID:34264001. Compared: Transvaginal mesh vs laparoscopic sacropexy for cystocele. Why it matters: Transvaginal mesh versus laparoscopic sacropexy for cystocele (Eur Urol 2018).
weber-anterior: Weber 2001 anterior colporrhaphy techniques (also: Weber 2001). Primary report: Weber AM, Walters MD, Piedmonte MR, et al. Anterior colporrhaphy: a randomized trial of three surgical techniques. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2001;185(6):1299-304. doi:10.1067/mob.2001.119081 PMID:11744900. Compared: Standard vs ultralateral colporrhaphy vs absorbable mesh. Why it matters: Three anterior colporrhaphy techniques (standard, ultralateral, absorbable mesh).
paraiso-rectocele: Paraiso 2006 rectocele repair techniques (also: Paraiso 2006). Primary report: Paraiso MF, Barber MD, Muir TW, et al. Rectocele repair: a randomized trial of three surgical techniques including graft augmentation. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2006;195(6):1762-71. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2006.07.026 PMID:17132479. Compared: Posterior colporrhaphy vs site-specific vs porcine graft. Why it matters: Three rectocele repairs including porcine graft augmentation; 2 WARWIKI pages cite it.
menefee-paravaginal: Menefee colporrhaphy versus mesh or graft paravaginal repair (also: Menefee 2011); NCT01393171. Primary report: Menefee SA, Dyer KY, Lukacz ES, et al. Colporrhaphy compared with mesh or graft-reinforced vaginal paravaginal repair for anterior vaginal wall prolapse: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;118(6):1337-1344. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e318237edc4 PMID:22067717. Compared: Colporrhaphy vs mesh or graft paravaginal repair. Why it matters: Colporrhaphy versus mesh- or graft-reinforced paravaginal repair.
prevprol: PREVPROL (also: PFMT for secondary prevention of prolapse); NCT01171846. Primary report: Hagen S, Glazener C, McClurg D, et al. Pelvic floor muscle training for secondary prevention of pelvic organ prolapse (PREVPROL): a multicentre randomised controlled trial. *Lancet.* 2017;389(10067):393-402. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(16)32109-2 PMID:28010994. Compared: PFMT vs leaflet after childbirth (prolapse prevention). Why it matters: PFMT for secondary prevention of prolapse after childbirth; cited in EAU female LUTS 2026.
cheung-pessary: Cheung pessary versus no treatment (also: Cheung 2016). Primary report: Cheung RY, Lee JH, Lee LL, et al. Vaginal Pessary in Women With Symptomatic Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Randomized Controlled Trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2016;128(1):73-80. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000001489 PMID:27275798. Compared: Pessary plus PFMT vs PFMT alone. Why it matters: Pessary versus no treatment for symptomatic prolapse; cited in EAU female LUTS 2026.
pessary-estrogen-zhou: Zhou intravaginal conjugated oestrogen with pessary (also: Zhou 2025); NCT04393194. Primary report: Zhou Y, Yin R, Zhang Y, et al. Effects of intravaginal conjugated oestrogen on pessary continuation for pelvic organ prolapse: multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial. *BMJ.* 2025;389:e084418. doi:10.1136/bmj-2025-084418 PMID:40578851. Compared: Vaginal conjugated oestrogen vs placebo with pessary. Why it matters: Vaginal conjugated oestrogen and pessary continuation (BMJ 2025); 6 WARWIKI pages cite it.
eva: EVA (also: Vaginal oestrogen before prolapse surgery (Netherlands)). Primary report: Vodegel EV, van Rest K, Speksnijder L, et al. Vaginal Oestrogen Therapy for Postmenopausal Women Undergoing Prolapse Surgery: A Multicentre Double-Blind Randomised Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial. *BJOG.* Published online August 28, 2026. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.70311 PMID:42663275. Compared: Vaginal oestrogen vs placebo before prolapse surgery. Why it matters: Dutch placebo-controlled trial of vaginal oestrogen before prolapse surgery, confirmatory to IMPROVE; 5 WARWIKI pages cite it. Note: Published online in BJOG in 2026; volume and pages not yet assigned.
recoup: ReCOUP (also: Activity restriction after reconstructive pelvic surgery); NCT02138487. Primary report: Mueller MG, Lewicky-Gaupp C, Collins SA, et al. Activity Restriction Recommendations and Outcomes After Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2017;129(4):608-614. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000001924 PMID:28277355. Later reports: Mueller MG, Collins SA, Lewicky-Gaupp C, et al. Restricted Convalescence Following Urogynecologic Procedures: 1-Year Outcomes From a Randomized Controlled Study. *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2021;27(2):e336-e341. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000000922 PMID:32947549. Compared: Liberal vs restricted activity after prolapse surgery. Why it matters: Liberal versus restricted activity after prolapse surgery.
expedited-activity: O'Shea standard restrictions versus expedited activity (also: O'Shea 2023); NCT04329715. Primary report: O'Shea M, Siddiqui NY, Truong T, et al. Standard Restrictions vs Expedited Activity After Pelvic Organ Prolapse Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA Surg.* 2023;158(8):797-805. doi:10.1001/jamasurg.2023.1649 PMID:37256578. Compared: Expedited activity vs standard restrictions after prolapse surgery. Why it matters: Standard restrictions versus expedited activity after prolapse surgery (JAMA Surg 2023).
geller-voiding-trial: Geller retrograde versus spontaneous voiding trial (also: Geller 2011); NCT01091844. Primary report: Geller EJ, Hankins KJ, Parnell BA, et al. Diagnostic accuracy of retrograde and spontaneous voiding trials for postoperative voiding dysfunction: a randomized controlled trial. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;118(3):637-642. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e318229e8dd PMID:21860294. Compared: Retrograde-fill vs spontaneous voiding trial. Why it matters: Retrograde-fill versus spontaneous voiding trial after pelvic surgery.
hakvoort-catheter: Hakvoort catheter duration after prolapse surgery (also: Hakvoort 2004). Primary report: Hakvoort RA, Elberink R, Vollebregt A, et al. How long should urinary bladder catheterisation be continued after vaginal prolapse surgery? A randomised controlled trial comparing short term versus long term catheterisation after vaginal prolapse surgery. *BJOG.* 2004;111(8):828-30. doi:10.1111/j.1471-0528.2004.00181.x PMID:15270931. Compared: Catheter removed after 1 day vs on day 5. Why it matters: Catheter removal timing after vaginal prolapse surgery.
pps-pivotal: Pentosan polysulfate pivotal trials (also: Elmiron, Mulholland 1990, Parsons 1993). Primary report: Mulholland SG, Hanno P, Parsons CL, et al. Pentosan polysulfate sodium for therapy of interstitial cystitis. A double-blind placebo-controlled clinical study. *Urology.* 1990;35(6):552-8. doi:10.1016/0090-4295(90)80116-5 PMID:1693797. Later reports: Parsons CL, Benson G, Childs SJ, et al. A quantitatively controlled method to study prospectively interstitial cystitis and demonstrate the efficacy of pentosanpolysulfate. *J Urol.* 1993;150(3):845-8. doi:10.1016/s0022-5347(17)35629-x PMID:7688432. Compared: Pentosan polysulfate vs placebo. Why it matters: Placebo-controlled trials behind FDA approval of pentosan polysulfate (Elmiron, 1996); AUA IC/BPS 2022 discusses both. No IC/BPS trial is in the library. Note: Two placebo-controlled trials that supported Elmiron approval.
pps-dose-nickel: Pentosan polysulfate dose and placebo trial (also: Nickel 2015). Primary report: Nickel JC, Herschorn S, Whitmore KE, et al. Pentosan polysulfate sodium for treatment of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome: insights from a randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled study. *J Urol.* 2015;193(3):857-62. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2014.09.036 PMID:25245489. Compared: Pentosan 100 mg daily vs three times daily vs placebo. Why it matters: Placebo-controlled pentosan dose trial with no benefit over placebo; cited in EAU chronic pelvic pain 2026.
icrn-amitriptyline: ICCRN amitriptyline trial (also: Foster 2010); NCT00124306. Primary report: Foster HE Jr, Hanno PM, Nickel JC, et al. Effect of amitriptyline on symptoms in treatment naïve patients with interstitial cystitis/painful bladder syndrome. *J Urol.* 2010;183(5):1853-8. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2009.12.106 PMID:20303115. Compared: Amitriptyline plus education vs placebo plus education. Why it matters: ICCRN amitriptyline trial in treatment-naive IC/BPS; cited in AUA IC/BPS 2022.
amitriptyline-van-ophoven: van Ophoven amitriptyline trial (also: van Ophoven 2004). Primary report: van Ophoven A, Pokupic S, Heinecke A, et al. A prospective, randomized, placebo controlled, double-blind study of amitriptyline for the treatment of interstitial cystitis. *J Urol.* 2004;172(2):533-6. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000132388.54703.4d PMID:15247722. Compared: Amitriptyline vs placebo. Why it matters: Placebo-controlled amitriptyline trial; cited in AUA IC/BPS 2022.
icctg-pps-hydroxyzine: ICCTG pentosan polysulfate and hydroxyzine trial (also: Sant 2003). Primary report: Sant GR, Propert KJ, Hanno PM, et al. A pilot clinical trial of oral pentosan polysulfate and oral hydroxyzine in patients with interstitial cystitis. *J Urol.* 2003;170(3):810-5. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000083020.06212.3d PMID:12913705. Compared: Pentosan, hydroxyzine, both, or placebo. Why it matters: ICCTG factorial trial of pentosan and hydroxyzine; cited in AUA IC/BPS 2022.
cyclosporine-ic: Cyclosporine A versus pentosan polysulfate (also: Sairanen 2005). Primary report: Sairanen J, Tammela TL, Leppilahti M, et al. Cyclosporine A and pentosan polysulfate sodium for the treatment of interstitial cystitis: a randomized comparative study. *J Urol.* 2005;174(6):2235-8. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000181808.45786.84 PMID:16280777. Compared: Cyclosporine A vs pentosan polysulfate. Why it matters: Cyclosporine A versus pentosan polysulfate; AUA IC/BPS 2022 cites it for refractory disease.
myofascial-pt-ic: Myofascial physical therapy trial (ICCRN) (also: FitzGerald 2012); NCT00733603. Primary report: FitzGerald MP, Payne CK, Lukacz ES, et al. Randomized multicenter clinical trial of myofascial physical therapy in women with interstitial cystitis/painful bladder syndrome and pelvic floor tenderness. *J Urol.* 2012;187(6):2113-8. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.01.123 PMID:22503015. Compared: Myofascial physical therapy vs global massage. Why it matters: Myofascial physical therapy versus global massage in IC/BPS; AUA IC/BPS 2022 cites it for manual physical therapy.
icctg-bcg: ICCTG intravesical BCG trial (also: Mayer 2005). Primary report: Mayer R, Propert KJ, Peters KM, et al. A randomized controlled trial of intravesical bacillus calmette-guerin for treatment refractory interstitial cystitis. *J Urol.* 2005;173(4):1186-91. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000152337.82806.e8 PMID:15758738. Compared: Intravesical BCG vs placebo. Why it matters: Negative intravesical BCG trial; AUA IC/BPS 2022 cites it.
dmso-ic: Perez-Marrero DMSO crossover trial (also: Perez-Marrero 1988). Primary report: Perez-Marrero R, Emerson LE, Feltis JT. A controlled study of dimethyl sulfoxide in interstitial cystitis. *J Urol.* 1988;140(1):36-9. doi:10.1016/s0022-5347(17)41478-9 PMID:3288775. Compared: Intravesical DMSO vs saline (crossover). Why it matters: Placebo-controlled DMSO crossover trial; AUA IC/BPS 2022 cites it.
botox-ic-kuo: Kuo intravesical botulinum toxin for IC/BPS (also: Kuo 2016). Primary report: Kuo HC, Jiang YH, Tsai YC, et al. Intravesical botulinum toxin-A injections reduce bladder pain of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome refractory to conventional treatment - A prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2016;35(5):609-14. doi:10.1002/nau.22760 PMID:25914337. Compared: Botulinum toxin A plus hydrodistension vs saline plus hydrodistension. Why it matters: Multicenter placebo-controlled intravesical onabotulinumtoxinA trial in IC/BPS.
rich-art: RICH-ART (also: Radiation-Induced Cystitis treated with Hyperbaric oxygen, A Randomised Trial); NCT01659723. Primary report: Oscarsson N, Müller B, Rosén A, et al. Radiation-induced cystitis treated with hyperbaric oxygen therapy (RICH-ART): a randomised, controlled, phase 2-3 trial. *Lancet Oncol.* 2019;20(11):1602-1614. doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(19)30494-2 PMID:31537473. Later reports: Oscarsson N, Rosén A, Müller B, et al. Radiation-induced cystitis treated with hyperbaric oxygen therapy (RICH-ART): long-term follow-up of a randomised controlled, phase 2-3 trial. *EClinicalMedicine.* 2025;83:103214. doi:10.1016/j.eclinm.2025.103214 PMID:40291346. Compared: Hyperbaric oxygen vs standard care for radiation cystitis. Why it matters: Hyperbaric oxygen for radiation cystitis (Lancet Oncol 2019; long-term 2025); 4 WARWIKI pages cite it.
gapp2: GaPP2 (also: Gabapentin for chronic pelvic pain in women). Primary report: Horne AW, Vincent K, Hewitt CA, et al. Gabapentin for chronic pelvic pain in women (GaPP2): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. *Lancet.* 2020;396(10255):909-917. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(20)31693-7 PMID:32979978. Compared: Gabapentin vs placebo, chronic pelvic pain in women. Why it matters: Gabapentin for chronic pelvic pain in women (negative); cited in EAU chronic pelvic pain 2026.
cpcrn-cipro-tamsulosin: CPCRN ciprofloxacin or tamsulosin trial (also: Alexander 2004). Primary report: Alexander RB, Propert KJ, Schaeffer AJ, et al. Ciprofloxacin or tamsulosin in men with chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome: a randomized, double-blind trial. *Ann Intern Med.* 2004;141(8):581-9. doi:10.7326/0003-4819-141-8-200410190-00005 PMID:15492337. Compared: Ciprofloxacin, tamsulosin, both, or placebo. Why it matters: CPCRN ciprofloxacin or tamsulosin for CP/CPPS (negative); cited in AUA male CPP 2025 and EAU.
pregabalin-cpps: CPCRN pregabalin trial (also: Pontari 2010); NCT00371033. Primary report: Pontari MA, Krieger JN, Litwin MS, et al. Pregabalin for the treatment of men with chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome: a randomized controlled trial. *Arch Intern Med.* 2010;170(17):1586-93. doi:10.1001/archinternmed.2010.319 PMID:20876412. Compared: Pregabalin vs placebo. Why it matters: CPCRN pregabalin trial; cited in AUA male CPP 2025 and EAU.
acupuncture-cpps: Sun acupuncture for CP/CPPS (also: Sun 2021); NCT03213938. Primary report: Sun Y, Liu Y, Liu B, et al. Efficacy of Acupuncture for Chronic Prostatitis/Chronic Pelvic Pain Syndrome : A Randomized Trial. *Ann Intern Med.* 2021;174(10):1357-1366. doi:10.7326/M21-1814 PMID:34399062. Compared: Acupuncture vs sham acupuncture. Why it matters: Sham-controlled acupuncture for CP/CPPS (Ann Intern Med 2021); cited in AUA male CPP 2025 and EAU.
antic: AnTIC (also: Continuous low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis in clean intermittent catheter users). Primary report: Fisher H, Oluboyede Y, Chadwick T, et al. Continuous low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis for adults with repeated urinary tract infections (AnTIC): a randomised, open-label trial. *Lancet Infect Dis.* 2018;18(9):957-968. doi:10.1016/S1473-3099(18)30279-2 PMID:30037647. Compared: Low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis vs none in CISC users. Why it matters: Low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis in intermittent-catheter users; cited in AUA/SUFU NLUTD 2021 and EAU female LUTS 2026.
raz-stamm-estriol: Raz and Stamm vaginal estriol trial (also: Raz 1993). Primary report: Raz R, Stamm WE. A controlled trial of intravaginal estriol in postmenopausal women with recurrent urinary tract infections. *N Engl J Med.* 1993;329(11):753-6. doi:10.1056/NEJM199309093291102 PMID:8350884. Compared: Vaginal estriol cream vs placebo. Why it matters: Vaginal estriol prevents recurrent UTI after menopause (NEJM 1993); cited in AUA rUTI 2025, AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM 2025 and NAMS.
hooton-water: Hooton increased water intake trial (also: Hooton 2018); NCT02444975. Primary report: Hooton TM, Vecchio M, Iroz A, et al. Effect of Increased Daily Water Intake in Premenopausal Women With Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections: A Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA Intern Med.* 2018;178(11):1509-1515. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2018.4204 PMID:30285042. Compared: Additional 1.5 L water daily vs usual intake. Why it matters: Increased water intake reduces recurrent cystitis; AUA rUTI 2025 cites it for fluid advice.
cai-asb: Cai asymptomatic bacteriuria treatment study (also: Cai 2012). Primary report: Cai T, Mazzoli S, Mondaini N, et al. The role of asymptomatic bacteriuria in young women with recurrent urinary tract infections: to treat or not to treat? *Clin Infect Dis.* 2012;55(6):771-7. doi:10.1093/cid/cis534 PMID:22677710. Later reports: Cai T, Nesi G, Mazzoli S, et al. Asymptomatic bacteriuria treatment is associated with a higher prevalence of antibiotic resistant strains in women with urinary tract infections. *Clin Infect Dis.* 2015;61(11):1655-61. doi:10.1093/cid/civ696 PMID:26270684. Compared: No treatment vs antibiotic treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria. Why it matters: Not treating asymptomatic bacteriuria in women with recurrent UTI; cited in AUA rUTI 2025 and EAU infections 2026. Note: PubMed indexes it as a clinical trial, not an RCT; the abstract says patients were 'split into 2 groups'. Check allocation in the full text before authoring.
stamm-1980: Stamm placebo-controlled prophylaxis trial (also: Stamm 1980). Primary report: Stamm WE, Counts GW, Wagner KF, et al. Antimicrobial prophylaxis of recurrent urinary tract infections: a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. *Ann Intern Med.* 1980;92(6):770-5. doi:10.7326/0003-4819-92-6-770 PMID:6992677. Compared: TMP-SMX, trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin prophylaxis vs placebo. Why it matters: Original placebo-controlled antimicrobial prophylaxis trial; cited in AUA rUTI 2025.
stapleton-postcoital: Stapleton postcoital prophylaxis trial (also: Stapleton 1990). Primary report: Stapleton A, Latham RH, Johnson C, et al. Postcoital antimicrobial prophylaxis for recurrent urinary tract infection. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. *JAMA.* 1990;264(6):703-6. doi:None PMID:2197450. Compared: Postcoital TMP-SMX vs placebo. Why it matters: Postcoital prophylaxis trial; cited in AUA rUTI 2025. Note: No DOI in PubMed.
impresu: ImpresU (also: Methenamine hippurate in older women); NCT04077580. Primary report: Heltveit-Olsen SR, Arnljots ES, Sundvall PD, et al. Methenamine hippurate as prophylaxis for recurrent urinary tract infections in older women-a triple-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase IV trial (ImpresU). *Clin Microbiol Infect.* 2025;31(11):1873-1879. doi:10.1016/j.cmi.2025.07.006 PMID:40669691. Compared: Methenamine hippurate vs placebo, older women. Why it matters: Placebo-controlled methenamine trial in older women (2025); 3 WARWIKI pages cite it.
botros-methenamine: Methenamine hippurate versus trimethoprim (also: Botros 2022). Primary report: Botros C, Lozo S, Iyer S, et al. Methenamine hippurate compared with trimethoprim for the prevention of recurrent urinary tract infections: a randomized clinical trial. *Int Urogynecol J.* 2022;33(3):571-580. doi:10.1007/s00192-021-04849-0 PMID:34115162. Compared: Methenamine hippurate vs trimethoprim. Why it matters: Methenamine versus trimethoprim; cited in AUA rUTI 2025.
napruti-cranberry: NAPRUTI cranberry versus TMP-SMX (also: Beerepoot 2011). Primary report: Beerepoot MA, ter Riet G, Nys S, et al. Cranberries vs antibiotics to prevent urinary tract infections: a randomized double-blind noninferiority trial in premenopausal women. *Arch Intern Med.* 2011;171(14):1270-8. doi:10.1001/archinternmed.2011.306 PMID:21788542. Compared: Cranberry capsules vs TMP-SMX. Why it matters: Cranberry versus TMP-SMX prophylaxis; cited in AUA rUTI 2025.
napruti-lactobacilli: NAPRUTI lactobacilli versus TMP-SMX (also: Beerepoot 2012). Primary report: Beerepoot MA, ter Riet G, Nys S, et al. Lactobacilli vs antibiotics to prevent urinary tract infections: a randomized, double-blind, noninferiority trial in postmenopausal women. *Arch Intern Med.* 2012;172(9):704-12. doi:10.1001/archinternmed.2012.777 PMID:22782199. Compared: Oral lactobacilli vs TMP-SMX. Why it matters: Oral lactobacilli versus TMP-SMX after menopause; cited in AUA rUTI 2025.
lactin-v: Lactin-V intravaginal Lactobacillus crispatus trial (also: Stapleton 2011); NCT00305227. Primary report: Stapleton AE, Au-Yeung M, Hooton TM, et al. Randomized, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial of a Lactobacillus crispatus probiotic given intravaginally for prevention of recurrent urinary tract infection. *Clin Infect Dis.* 2011;52(10):1212-7. doi:10.1093/cid/cir183 PMID:21498386. Compared: Intravaginal Lactobacillus crispatus vs placebo. Why it matters: Intravaginal Lactobacillus crispatus probiotic; cited in AUA rUTI 2025.
mv140: MV140 sublingual bacterial vaccine trial (also: Uromune, Lorenzo-Gómez 2022); NCT02543827. Primary report: Lorenzo-Gómez MF, Foley S, Nickel JC, et al. Sublingual MV140 for Prevention of Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections. *NEJM Evid.* 2022;1(4):EVIDoa2100018. doi:10.1056/EVIDoa2100018 PMID:38319200. Compared: Sublingual MV140 (3 or 6 months) vs placebo. Why it matters: Sublingual bacterial vaccine (NEJM Evid 2022); cited in AUA rUTI 2025.
om-89: OM-89 (Uro-Vaxom) long-term trial (also: Bauer 2005). Primary report: Bauer HW, Alloussi S, Egger G, et al. A long-term, multicenter, double-blind study of an Escherichia coli extract (OM-89) in female patients with recurrent urinary tract infections. *Eur Urol.* 2005;47(4):542-8. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2004.12.009 PMID:15774256. Compared: Oral E. coli lysate vs placebo. Why it matters: Oral E. coli lysate (OM-89) long-term trial; basis for EAU immunoprophylaxis statements.
ferrante-vaginal-estrogen: Ferrante vaginal estrogen RCT (also: Ferrante 2021); NCT01958073. Primary report: Ferrante KL, Wasenda EJ, Jung CE, et al. Vaginal Estrogen for the Prevention of Recurrent Urinary Tract Infection in Postmenopausal Women: A Randomized Clinical Trial. *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2021;27(2):112-117. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000000749 PMID:31232721. Compared: Vaginal estrogen vs placebo. Why it matters: Contemporary vaginal estrogen RCT for recurrent UTI; cited in AUA rUTI 2025 and AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM 2025.
eriksen-estring: Eriksen estradiol vaginal ring trial (also: Estring, Eriksen 1999). Primary report: Eriksen B. A randomized, open, parallel-group study on the preventive effect of an estradiol-releasing vaginal ring (Estring) on recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 1999;180(5):1072-9. doi:10.1016/s0002-9378(99)70597-1 PMID:10329858. Compared: Estradiol vaginal ring vs no treatment. Why it matters: Estradiol vaginal ring for recurrent UTI; cited in AUA rUTI 2025, AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM 2025 and NAMS.
compare-catheters: COMPARE (also: Single-use versus reusable intermittent catheters). Primary report: van Veen FEE, Christiaans CHH, Berendsen SA, et al. Single-Use vs Reusable Catheters for Intermittent Catheterization in Patients With Urinary Retention: The COMPARE Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA Netw Open.* 2026;9(6):e2620871. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20871 PMID:42377956. Compared: Reusable vs single-use intermittent catheters. Why it matters: Single-use versus reusable intermittent catheters (JAMA Netw Open 2026); 2 WARWIKI pages cite it.
hydrophilic-catheter-sci: Cardenas hydrophilic catheter trial in acute SCI (also: Cardenas 2011). Primary report: Cardenas DD, Moore KN, Dannels-McClure A, et al. Intermittent catheterization with a hydrophilic-coated catheter delays urinary tract infections in acute spinal cord injury: a prospective, randomized, multicenter trial. *PM R.* 2011;3(5):408-17. doi:10.1016/j.pmrj.2011.01.001 PMID:21570027. Compared: Hydrophilic vs uncoated catheters in acute SCI. Why it matters: Hydrophilic versus uncoated catheters after acute SCI; cited in AUA/SUFU NLUTD 2021.
ospemifene-pivotal: Ospemifene pivotal trials (also: Osphena, Bachmann 2010, Portman 2013). Primary report: Bachmann GA, Komi JO. Ospemifene effectively treats vulvovaginal atrophy in postmenopausal women: results from a pivotal phase 3 study. *Menopause.* 2010;17(3):480-6. doi:10.1097/gme.0b013e3181c1ac01 PMID:20032798. Later reports: Portman DJ, Bachmann GA, Simon JA. Ospemifene, a novel selective estrogen receptor modulator for treating dyspareunia associated with postmenopausal vulvar and vaginal atrophy. *Menopause.* 2013;20(6):623-30. doi:10.1097/gme.0b013e318279ba64 PMID:23361170. Compared: Ospemifene 30 or 60 mg vs placebo. Why it matters: Ospemifene registration trials (Osphena, FDA 2013); cited in AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM 2025 and NAMS. No GSM trial is in the library.
prasterone-pivotal: Prasterone (intravaginal DHEA) pivotal trial (also: Intrarosa, Labrie 2016). Primary report: Labrie F, Archer DF, Koltun W, et al. Efficacy of intravaginal dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) on moderate to severe dyspareunia and vaginal dryness, symptoms of vulvovaginal atrophy, and of the genitourinary syndrome of menopause. *Menopause.* 2016;23(3):243-56. doi:10.1097/GME.0000000000000571 PMID:26731686. Compared: Intravaginal prasterone vs placebo. Why it matters: Intravaginal prasterone registration trial (Intrarosa, FDA 2016).
rejoice: REJOICE (also: TX-004HR estradiol vaginal insert, Imvexxy). Primary report: Constantine GD, Simon JA, Pickar JH, et al. The REJOICE trial: a phase 3 randomized, controlled trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of a novel vaginal estradiol soft-gel capsule for symptomatic vulvar and vaginal atrophy. *Menopause.* 2017;24(4):409-416. doi:10.1097/GME.0000000000000786 PMID:27922936. Compared: Estradiol vaginal insert 4, 10 or 25 µg vs placebo. Why it matters: Estradiol vaginal insert registration trial (Imvexxy, FDA 2018); cited in AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM 2025.
vagifem-10: Ultra-low-dose estradiol vaginal tablet trial (also: Vagifem 10 mcg, Simon 2008); NCT00108849. Primary report: Simon J, Nachtigall L, Gut R, et al. Effective treatment of vaginal atrophy with an ultra-low-dose estradiol vaginal tablet. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2008;112(5):1053-60. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e31818aa7c3 PMID:18978105. Compared: Estradiol 10 µg vaginal tablet vs placebo. Why it matters: Registration trial for the 10 µg estradiol vaginal tablet; cited in NAMS 2020.
msflash-vaginal: Mitchell vaginal estradiol or moisturizer versus placebo (also: Mitchell 2018, MsFLASH); NCT02516202. Primary report: Mitchell CM, Reed SD, Diem S, et al. Efficacy of Vaginal Estradiol or Vaginal Moisturizer vs Placebo for Treating Postmenopausal Vulvovaginal Symptoms: A Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA Intern Med.* 2018;178(5):681-690. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2018.0116 PMID:29554173. Compared: Vaginal estradiol vs moisturizer vs placebo gel. Why it matters: MsFLASH trial of vaginal estradiol or moisturizer versus placebo gel (no difference); cited in AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM 2025 and NAMS.
laser-sham-li: Li fractional CO2 laser versus sham (also: Li 2021). Primary report: Li FG, Maheux-Lacroix S, Deans R, et al. Effect of Fractional Carbon Dioxide Laser vs Sham Treatment on Symptom Severity in Women With Postmenopausal Vaginal Symptoms: A Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA.* 2021;326(14):1381-1389. doi:10.1001/jama.2021.14892 PMID:34636862. Compared: Fractional CO2 laser vs sham. Why it matters: Fractional CO2 laser no better than sham for postmenopausal vaginal symptoms (JAMA 2021); cited in AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM 2025.
laser-vs-estrogen-paraiso: Paraiso vaginal laser versus vaginal estrogen (also: Paraiso 2020); NCT02691936. Primary report: Paraiso MFR, Ferrando CA, Sokol ER, et al. A randomized clinical trial comparing vaginal laser therapy to vaginal estrogen therapy in women with genitourinary syndrome of menopause: The VeLVET Trial. *Menopause.* 2020;27(1):50-56. doi:10.1097/GME.0000000000001416 PMID:31574047. Compared: Vaginal CO2 laser vs vaginal estrogen cream. Why it matters: Vaginal laser versus vaginal estrogen; cited in AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM 2025 and NAMS.
maps: MAPS (also: Men After Prostate Surgery). Primary report: Glazener C, Boachie C, Buckley B, et al. Urinary incontinence in men after formal one-to-one pelvic-floor muscle training following radical prostatectomy or transurethral resection of the prostate (MAPS): two parallel randomised controlled trials. *Lancet.* 2011;378(9788):328-37. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(11)60751-4 PMID:21741700. Later reports: Glazener C, Boachie C, Buckley B, et al. Conservative treatment for urinary incontinence in Men After Prostate Surgery (MAPS): two parallel randomised controlled trials. *Health Technol Assess.* 2011;15(24):1-290, iii-iv. doi:10.3310/hta15240 PMID:21640056. Compared: One-to-one PFMT vs standard care after prostatectomy or TURP. Why it matters: PFMT after radical prostatectomy or TURP (Lancet 2011); cited in EAU male LUTS 2026. The male-SUI timeline has no conservative-care trial.
goode-2011: Goode 2011 behavioral therapy for persistent postprostatectomy incontinence (also: Goode 2011); NCT00212264. Primary report: Goode PS, Burgio KL, Johnson TM 2nd, et al. Behavioral therapy with or without biofeedback and pelvic floor electrical stimulation for persistent postprostatectomy incontinence: a randomized controlled trial. *JAMA.* 2011;305(2):151-9. doi:10.1001/jama.2010.1972 PMID:21224456. Compared: Behavioral therapy with or without biofeedback and stimulation vs delayed treatment. Why it matters: Behavioral therapy with or without biofeedback and stimulation for persistent post-prostatectomy incontinence; cited in AUA IPT 2024 and EAU.
pless: PLESS (also: Proscar Long-term Efficacy and Safety Study). Primary report: McConnell JD, Bruskewitz R, Walsh P, et al. The effect of finasteride on the risk of acute urinary retention and the need for surgical treatment among men with benign prostatic hyperplasia. Finasteride Long-Term Efficacy and Safety Study Group. *N Engl J Med.* 1998;338(9):557-63. doi:10.1056/NEJM199802263380901 PMID:9475762. Compared: Finasteride vs placebo, 4 years. Why it matters: Finasteride reduced acute retention and BPH surgery (NEJM 1998); cited in AUA BPH 2026 and EAU male LUTS 2026.
va-coop-bph: VA Cooperative BPH trial (also: Veterans Affairs Cooperative Studies Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Study Group, Lepor 1996). Primary report: Lepor H, Williford WO, Barry MJ, et al. The efficacy of terazosin, finasteride, or both in benign prostatic hyperplasia. Veterans Affairs Cooperative Studies Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Study Group. *N Engl J Med.* 1996;335(8):533-9. doi:10.1056/NEJM199608223350801 PMID:8684407. Compared: Terazosin vs finasteride vs both vs placebo. Why it matters: Terazosin, finasteride or both (NEJM 1996); cited in EAU male LUTS 2026; the forerunner of MTOPS.
aria-dutasteride: Dutasteride ARIA pivotal trials (also: ARIA3001, ARIA3002, ARIA3003, Roehrborn 2002). Primary report: Roehrborn CG, Boyle P, Nickel JC, et al. Efficacy and safety of a dual inhibitor of 5-alpha-reductase types 1 and 2 (dutasteride) in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia. *Urology.* 2002;60(3):434-41. doi:10.1016/s0090-4295(02)01905-2 PMID:12350480. Compared: Dutasteride vs placebo, 2 years. Why it matters: Dutasteride registration trials (FDA 2001); cited in AUA BPH 2026 and EAU. Note: Pooled report of the three ARIA phase 3 trials.
tamsulosin-pivotal: Tamsulosin US pivotal trials (also: Lepor 1998, Narayan 1998). Primary report: Lepor H. Phase III multicenter placebo-controlled study of tamsulosin in benign prostatic hyperplasia. Tamsulosin Investigator Group. *Urology.* 1998;51(6):892-900. doi:10.1016/s0090-4295(98)00126-5 PMID:9609623. Later reports: Narayan P, Tewari A. A second phase III multicenter placebo controlled study of 2 dosages of modified release tamsulosin in patients with symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia. United States 93-01 Study Group. *J Urol.* 1998;160(5):1701-6. PMID:9783935. Compared: Tamsulosin 0.4 or 0.8 mg vs placebo. Why it matters: Tamsulosin US registration trials (FDA 1997). Note: Narayan 1998 has no DOI in PubMed.
silodosin-pivotal: Silodosin US pivotal trials (also: Marks 2009); ['NCT00224107', 'NCT00224120']. Primary report: Marks LS, Gittelman MC, Hill LA, et al. Rapid efficacy of the highly selective alpha1A-adrenoceptor antagonist silodosin in men with signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia: pooled results of 2 phase 3 studies. *J Urol.* 2009;181(6):2634-40. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2009.02.034 PMID:19371887. Compared: Silodosin 8 mg vs placebo. Why it matters: Silodosin US registration trials (FDA 2008).
